A 25 bp cut with guidance to maintain ample reserves via T‑bill purchases and repo operations signals a mildly accommodative stance. With inflation running below 2% and business fixed investment and exports weak, the move is consistent with inflation-targeting principles that advocate easing when inflation and activity are soft (Svensson). New Keynesian evidence linking inflation to real marginal cost (Galí, Gertler, and López-Salido) and VAR studies showing near-term real effects of monetary policy shocks (Sims; Zha; B. Friedman) support the Committee’s aim to sustain expansion and nudge inflation toward target. Given investment’s role in business-cycle fluctuations and GDP (investment functions influencing firms and explaining fluctuations), easing can help offset weak capex. The Desk’s operating choices to ensure ample reserves align with research on operating procedures and the monetary base. Still, low market-based inflation compensation and dissenting votes warrant caution. Overall tone: mildly positive/dovish.
